recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future desire for explicit child-and-self or leaf-and-self operators, or for descendent/descendant spelling changes, should be handled as a new Vocabulary WG terminology decision rather than as FHIR-23783 reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-23783 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Vocabulary WG R5 change request for FHIR-core ValueSet. It requested FilterOperator additions for VSD DirectRelationsOnly with IncludeHeadCode=false and TransitiveClosureLeaves with IncludeHeadCode=false, while supporting the corresponding IncludeHeadCode=true cases by adding a separate ValueSet.compose include for the head code itself.
initial_application: The R5 application occurred through vocabulary history: 054eabf3116825c0f65107fedff6668447bf43a1 added child-of after an earlier reverted attempt, b0172dd266bc5061422826c714e77a6d3c559296 explicitly listed FHIR-23783 and added the leaf operator, and 732b40c16876bd7f23e75b50253824d920485f4e corrected that code to descendent-leaf while adding the matching narrative row.
additional_context: ValueSet is active in source/fhir.ini, and the ValueSet and CodeSystem structure definitions list child-of and descendent-leaf in the required FilterOperator binding summaries. R5 history contains the codes while R4/R4B history does not. Related FHIR-36644 reused these operators in CodeSystem concept-filter guidance and is already represented on the combined branch; FHIR-39264 and FHIR-49057 support preserving descendent-family normative spellings.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because source/valueset/codesystem-filter-operator.xml defines the two requested operators and source/valueset/valueset-filter-operator.xml includes the complete filter-operator code system.

related_jiras.note: Later CodeSystem filter guidance uses the same child-of and descendent-leaf operators and is already represented on the combined branch.
Later technical correction around descendent spelling/punctuation confirms corrections should be narrow and preserve normative code spellings.
Later no-change response confirms descendent-of spelling cannot be renamed because it is normative/backward-compatible.
